info.name: Miqaat Embedded Login - Existing Databases
info.description:
End-to-end Embedded Login -> Authentication (existing identity database) -> Authorization (existing authorization database).

Uses only EXISTING users, roles and permissions. No request creates or changes a user, role, tenant, module or permission; the services only write their own session / login-attempt / audit rows.

Run the folders in order (Collection Runner or `newman run`). Select the environment first and fill in existing ITS IDs and passwords:
- memberItsId / memberPassword: active, eligible, allow_login, present in the authorization DB with ONE role (tenant-scoped role recommended)
- multiRoleItsId: holds several roles
- ineligibleItsId: not in user_eligible; inactiveItsId: status_id <> 3; notAllowedItsId: allow_login = false
- notOnboardedItsId: not in the authorization users table; disabledItsId: authorization users.status = DISABLED; noRoleItsId: no role
- otherTenantId: any tenant id different from the member role's tenant; deniedModule: a module code the member role has no grant on

Scenario requests whose ITS ID variable is empty will fail - remove them from the run if you have no such user.
Requests that go straight to the services imitate the browser (iframe fetch-metadata headers, Origin, CSRF) exactly as the React embed app sends them.

Portal (workspace) login. Needs the authorization service catalog APIs; not part of the embedded-login flow.

Authenticates like embedded login, then asks the authorization service for workspaces. Core Portal workspace login. It depends on catalog APIs that were removed from core-authorization (they read tables the existing admin_db does not have), so it cannot succeed against admin_db.

item.name: 8. Authorization service - remaining endpoints
item.description:
The rest of core-authorization. The session endpoints used by Embedded Login are in folders 3-5.

The catalog and admin APIs (clients, origins, callbacks, applications, business units, utilities, environments, modules, roles, users, me, authorization check / effective-permissions / token, internal federation) were removed from the service: they read tables the existing admin_db does not contain.
